# ML Evaluation Report (auto-generated)

Generated by `scripts/ml_report.py`. All numbers below were computed by that script.

## 1. Dataset (EDA)

* Training corpus: `phishing_synthetic.csv` - **synthetic, template-generated** (see `scripts/generate_sample_data.py`).
* Rows: 600 (after de-duplication used for training: 314)
* Class balance: {'phishing': 300, 'legitimate': 300}
* Text length (chars): mean 195, min 163, max 226
* Distinct texts: 314 of 600 - a small template space, so train/test overlap in *style* is unavoidable.

Most phishing-indicative terms (logistic-regression weights): `be`, `will`, `now`, `your`, `claim`, `payment`, `in`, `unusual`, `action`, `password`

Most legitimate-indicative terms: `for`, `thanks`, `thanks for`, `for your`, `have`, `review`, `schedule`, `spreadsheet`, `report`, `draft`

## 2. Features & model

* Text: TF-IDF (unigrams+bigrams, min_df=2, sublinear tf) -> Logistic Regression (class_weight=balanced, seed 42).
* Deterministic features (not learned): sender look-alike, risky TLD, URL structure, urgency/credential/threat language, auth results (see `services/phishing.py`).
* Final verdict = deterministic points + at most 25 ML points; ML alone can never yield `phishing`.

## 3. Phishing text model

| Evaluation set | n | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | FPR | Confusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Synthetic held-out (75/25 stratified) | 79 | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 | 0.0 | TN 39 FP 0 FN 0 TP 40 |
| Hand-written (never trained on) | 16 | 0.8125 | 0.7778 | 0.875 | 0.8235 | 0.25 | TN 6 FP 2 FN 1 TP 7 |

**Interpretation.** The synthetic held-out score is near-perfect because train and test come from the same templates; it is *not* evidence of real-world accuracy. The 16-email hand-written set is a more honest but tiny check (wide uncertainty). Misclassified: "IT helpdesk: your VPN certificate is invalid. Reply with your username and passw..."; "Urgent: the staging server will be restarted tonight at 10pm for maintenance. Pl..."; "Security notice: we recommend enabling two-factor authentication. You can do thi...".

## 4. Full phishing analyser (deterministic + ML), body text only

On the same 16 hand-written texts (no sender/URL supplied, 'suspicious' counted as flagged): TP 5, FP 0, TN 8, FN 3. Errors: Action required: your Microsoft 365 password expires in 2 ho; Dear user, a payment of 849.00 was authorised from your acco; Unusual sign-in attempt detected from a new device. Click he.

## 5. Log detection on the synthetic sample (known ground truth)

Sample: 274 events, 3 injected attack scenarios (brute force + success, password spraying, off-hours privileged activity) among ~220 normal events.

| Injected scenario | Detected by rules |
|---|---|
| brute_force | yes |
| password_spraying | yes |
| sensitive_activity_off_hours | yes |

* Rule alerts: 5; false brute-force/spraying alerts on normal internal traffic: 0.
* Isolation Forest windows flagged: 10 of 216 (contamination fixed at 5%), producing 5 low-severity ML alerts. Because contamination is a fixed fraction, the model **always** flags ~5% of windows - these are anomaly *signals*, expected to include benign activity, and are labelled unconfirmed in reports.

**Caveat.** The scenarios were generated by the same author as the detection rules, so this is a functional check, not an accuracy benchmark. No evaluation on CIC-IDS2017, UNSW-NB15 or other public datasets was performed (see LIMITATIONS.md).
